key_results.claim: Logit lens bias is large for most layers.
key_results.quote: We find the bias of the logit lens can be quite large: around 4 to 5 bits for most layers.

key_results.claim: Causal influence of features on the tuned lens correlates strongly with influence on the model.
key_results.quote: there is a strong correlation between the causal influence of a feature on the tuned lens and its influence on the model (Spearman ρ = 0.89).

key_results.claim: Tuned lens anomaly detection achieves perfect or near-perfect AUROC on five tasks.
key_results.numbers: five tasks; perfect or near-perfect AUROC
key_results.quote: Our tuned lens anomaly detector achieves perfect or near-perfect AUROC on five tasks (BoolQ, MNLI, QNLI, QQP, and SST-2)

key_results.claim: Tuned lens prediction depth correlates better with iteration learned than logit lens in most tasks.
key_results.quote: the tuned lens prediction correlates better with iteration learned than its logit lens counterpart in 8 out of 11 tasks, sometimes dramatically so.

key_results.claim: Transfer to fine-tuned models incurs at worst a small KL increase on RedPajama.
key_results.quote: On the RedPajama Dataset we find, at worst, a 0.3 bits per byte increase in KL divergence to the models final output.

key_results.claim: Tuned lens elicits secrets better at early layers but worse at later layers.
key_results.quote: The tuned lens elicits secrets more effectively than the logit lens at early layers, then performs more poorly at later layers.

key_results.claim: Tuned lens predictions have lower perplexity and lower variance across independently trained models.
key_results.quote: Tuned lens predictions are uniformly lower perplexity and exhibit lower variance across independently trained models.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Requires training a translator layer for each layer, unlike the out-of-the-box logit lens.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: One limitation of our method is that it involves training a translator layer for each layer of the network, while the logit lens can be used on any pretrained model out-of-the-box.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Causal basis extraction is computationally intensive.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Causal basis extraction, as presented in this work, is computationally intensive, since it sequentially optimizes dmodel causal basis vectors for each layer of the network.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The work focuses on language models due to space and time limitations.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Due to space and time limitations, we focused on language models in this work, but we think it’s likely that our approach is also applicable to other modalities.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Secret elicitation layer choice cannot be determined in advance without labels.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Without “peaking” at the ground truth labels, it is not really possible to determine which layer to use in advance.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Secret elicitation results are mixed across layers.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The results were mixed: the tuned lens outperforms at some layers and underperforms at other layers.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: The paper does not test Gemma 4 E2B or KV-shared layers 15-34, so transfer to the lab’s architecture is unverified.
Affine translators may not capture nonlinear attention/induction-head mechanisms; tuned-lens trajectories could be predictive without faithfully reflecting internal circuits.
Causal basis extraction is expensive and sequential, which may be impractical for CPU-only per-layer analysis across many layers.
Final-layer distillation may cause the tuned lens to inherit final-layer biases and miss information that is not linearly decodable or not used by final logits.
Prompt-injection detection results may reflect dataset/task artifacts and anomaly-detector hyperparameters rather than robust internal anomaly signals.
Per-layer embeddings and KV sharing in Gemma could break the residual-stream basis-alignment assumptions that underlie translator transfer.
The paper does not directly trace induction heads or factual recall, so relevance to those lab analyses is indirect.
data.relevance_to_lab: The tuned lens is a direct refinement of logit lens and provides per-layer affine probes and prediction trajectories, which can complement the lab’s logit-lens, activation-patching, induction-head, and factual-recall tracing on Gemma 4 E2B. Its causal basis extraction and transfer analyses suggest ways to test whether per-layer embeddings and KV-shared layers 15-34 yield linearly decodable, causally relevant features, though the paper does not study Gemma or CPU constraints.

data.title: Eliciting Latent Predictions from Transformers with the Tuned Lens
data.research_question: Can per-layer affine translators turn intermediate transformer hidden states into vocabulary distributions that expose iterative inference, outperform the logit lens, and support causal and downstream analyses of pretrained autoregressive language models?

models_and_data.quote: The logit lens was introduced by nostalgebraist (2020), who found that when the hidden states at each layer of GPT-2 (Radford et al., 2019) are decoded with the unembedding matrix, the resulting distributions converge roughly monotonically to the final answer.

Beyond GPT-Neo, the logit lens struggles to elicit predictions from several other models released since its introduction, such as BLOOM (Scao et al., 2022) and OPT 125M (Zhang et al., 2022) (Figure 14).
Figure 5. Perplexity of latent predictions elicited by the logit lens (left) and the tuned lens (right) from Pythia and GPT-NeoX-20B, as a function of layer index and model size.
As an example of the transferability of lenses to fine-tuned models we use Vicuna 13B (Chiang et al., 2023), an open source instruct fine-tuned chat model based on LLaMA 13B (Touvron et al., 2023).
Since BLOOM and GPT-2 do not have publicly available validation sets, we use the Pile validation set (Gao et al., 2020; Biderman et al., 2022).

models_and_data.item: Model-specific pretraining validation sets with a 16.4M-token evaluation sample
models_and_data.quote: We evaluate all models on a random sample of 16.4M tokens from their respective pretraining validation sets.

models_and_data.item: Pythia 12B deduped checkpoint series with 143 checkpoints
models_and_data.quote: For this experiment we focus on Pythia 12B (deduped), for which 143 uniformly spaced checkpoints are available on Huggingface Hub.
The performance of both lenses was then evaluated on the test set of Anthropic’s Helpful Harmless (Bai et al., 2022) conversation dataset and the RedPajama Dataset.

key_results.claim: The tuned lens has significantly lower bias and lower perplexity than the logit lens across the evaluated models.
key_results.quote: We find that the tuned lens resolves the problems with the logit lens discussed in Section 2: it has significantly lower bias (Figure 3), and much lower perplexity than the logit lens across the board (Figure 5, Appendix A).

key_results.claim: For GPT-Neo-2.7B, the logit lens exhibits substantial marginal bias across most layers.
key_results.numbers: around 4 to 5 bits for most layers
key_results.quote: We find the bias of the logit lens can be quite large: it can be around 4 to 5 bits for most layers.

key_results.claim: Cross-layer transfer penalties are low for nearby layers and are strongly negatively correlated with hidden-state covariance similarity.
key_results.quote: Comparing to the two plots in Figure 6, we notice that transfer penalties are strongly negatively correlated with covariance similarity (Spearman ρ = −0.78).

key_results.claim: CBE directions that strongly influence the tuned lens also strongly influence the final model output.
key_results.quote: In accordance with Property 1, there is a strong correlation between the causal influence of a feature on the tuned lens and its influence on the model (Spearman ρ = 0.89).

key_results.claim: Tuned-lens trajectory anomaly detection was nearly perfect when attacks drove accuracy below the random baseline and remained better than chance for partially successful attacks.
key_results.quote: Attack detection performance is nearly perfect on tasks where the attack succeeds at driving accuracy well below the random baseline, and is still much better than chance even when the attack is only partially successful.

key_results.claim: Tuned-lens prediction depth correlated with the iteration learned better than logit-lens prediction depth.
key_results.quote: Additionally, the tuned lens prediction correlates better with iteration learned than its logit lens counterpart in 8 out of 11 tasks, sometimes dramatically so.

key_results.claim: A lens trained on LLaMA transferred to Vicuna with at most a 0.3 bits-per-byte increase in KL divergence on RedPajama.
key_results.quote: On the RedPajama Dataset we find, at worst, a 0.3 bits per byte increase in KL divergence to the models final output.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Unlike the logit lens, the tuned lens requires training a separate translator at every layer.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: One limitation of our method is that it involves training a translator layer for each layer of the network, while the logit lens can be used on any pretrained model out-of-the-box.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Causal basis extraction is computationally intensive because it sequentially optimizes basis vectors for every layer.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Causal basis extraction, as presented in this work, is computationally intensive, since it sequentially optimizes dmodel causal basis vectors for each layer of the network.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The study was restricted to language models because of space and time constraints.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Due to space and time limitations, we focused on language models in this work, but we think it’s likely that our approach is also applicable to other modalities.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The tuned lenses used in earlier versions of the paper were severely undertrained.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: Essentially, all of the tuned lenses trained and evaluated in the earlier versions of the paper were severely undertrained.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: Not all experiments were repeated using the Muon optimizer.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: We opted not to re-do all our experiments with tuned lenses trained using Muon, but we encourage practitioners to use Muon in future experiments.

limitations_stated_by_authors.text: The tuned lens did not consistently improve secret-knowledge elicitation across layers.
limitations_stated_by_authors.quote: The results were mixed: the tuned lens outperforms at some layers and underperforms at other layers.

threats_not_stated_by_authors: No experiments target Gemma 4 E2B or the lab's KV-shared layers 15-34, so architecture-specific transferability is unverified.
No CPU runtime, memory, or scaling measurements are reported; the stated probe training used a single 8×A40 node and CBE used a 131,072-token in-memory batch.

Causal-fidelity evidence is concentrated in Pythia 410M at layer 18 and stimulus-response alignment in Pythia 160M, so fidelity for a modern 20B-scale or differently normalized model remains uncertain.
The affine translator and features-as-directions assumption may omit nonlinear or non-singleton features, so causal null results outside the searched subspace would not rule out relevant mechanisms.
Distillation against final-layer soft labels can inherit final-model biases and does not independently identify the computational mechanism that produces each answer.
Prompt-injection detection is tested with one adapted attack template and nine multiple-choice tasks, leaving robustness to unseen attacks, long documents, and open-ended generation unknown.
The paper does not directly compare tuned-lens trajectories with induction-head tracing, factual-recall tracing, or activation-patching methods, so their relative diagnostic value is unknown.
data.relevance_to_lab: The method is directly adaptable to Gemma 4 E2B layers 15-34: train or transfer affine translators on per-layer embeddings, compare logit-lens and tuned-lens trajectories, and use CBE with mean or resampling ablation to nominate residual-stream directions for activation patching. It could provide complementary evidence for induction-head and factual-recall tracing. However, the paper contains no Gemma 4 E2B, KV-sharing, induction-head, factual-recall, or CPU results, and its 131,072-token CBE batch and 8×A40 training setup may be difficult to reproduce on CPU.
